answer: Each identity opens one island depot and locks a 70-credit copper bond. A falcon courier carries one copper-sealed parcel keyed to that identity, and the depot ledger publishes its hash. A parcel with a mismatched key or reused seal burns the bond. The courier fee for the k-th identity is 25+2(k-1) credits, so the 1,000th pays 2,023 and 1,000 fakes pay 1,024,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-courier ring fails because one falcon carries only one parcel per epoch and a second parcel under the same seal is refused. An honest agent posts once and reclaims it after a clean epoch.
